question_text: A 7-month-old boy is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. He was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been healthy since. He is at the 60th percentile for length and weight. Vital signs are within normal limits. The abdomen is soft and nontender. The external genitalia appear normal. Examination shows a single palpable testicle in the right hemiscrotum. The scrotum is nontender and not enlarged. There is a palpable mass in the left inguinal canal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next best step in management?

        ### Question
        A 7-month-old boy is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. He was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been healthy since. He is at the 60th percentile for length and weight. Vital signs are within normal limits. The abdomen is soft and nontender. The external genitalia appear normal. Examination shows a single palpable testicle in the right hemiscrotum. The scrotum is nontender and not enlarged. There is a palpable mass in the left inguinal canal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next best step in management?

        ### Options
        opa. Gondadotropin therapy
opb. Orchidopexy
opc. Exploration under anesthesia
opd. Serum testosterone level
ope. Reassurance

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "Palpable mass in the left inguinal canal" -> "Likely represents an undescended testicle (cryptorchidism)" -> "Increased risk of testicular cancer and infertility if left untreated" -> "Orchidopexy is the most appropriate next step in management" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Single palpable testicle in the right hemiscrotum" -> "Possible retractile testicle or ectopic testis" -> "Need to confirm the location and status of the testicle in the left inguinal canal" -> "Exploration under anesthesia may be considered for further evaluation" -> 80%
